stem: A surveillance team already knows which patients truly had a disease from an independent assessment. It asks how successfully a new case definition identifies those patients. Which of the following quantities directly evaluates this goal?

options.label: A
options.text: False positive results divided by all positive results
options.explanation: This asks how many positive results are false alarms. Sensitivity instead starts with all people known to have disease and measures how many the definition detects.
options.misconception: Counts false alarms among positive results instead of detected actual cases.

options.label: B
options.text: True negative results divided by all negative results
options.explanation: This starts with negative results and measures how many are truly disease-free. The surveillance question instead concerns detection among the independently established group with disease.
options.misconception: Uses the negative-result denominator rather than the actual-case group.

options.label: C
options.text: True negative results divided by all disease-free patients
options.explanation: This is specificity: correctly excluding disease among people without it. Sensitivity uses the group with disease as the denominator and counts the cases detected.
options.misconception: Confuses exclusion among noncases with detection among cases.

options.label: D
options.text: True positive results divided by all people with disease
options.explanation: Sensitivity is the proportion of true cases identified by a test or case definition. Divide the detected true cases by all independently established cases to evaluate this goal.
options.misconception: No misconception: sensitivity counts detected true cases among all actual cases.

options.label: E
options.text: True positive results divided by all positive results
options.explanation: This is positive predictive value, which evaluates whether positive results represent disease. Sensitivity evaluates how many actual cases are detected, so its denominator is all patients with disease.
options.misconception: Substitutes the PPV positive-result denominator for all people with disease.

context:
Learning objective: Identify the actual-case denominator for sensitivity before calculating case detection.

Sensitivity is the proportion of true cases identified by a test or case definition. Divide the detected true cases by all independently established cases to evaluate this goal.
